name: Badging API
plain: Shows a number or dot on an installed app icon.
meaning: Puts an unread count on the app icon of an installed web app. No prompt on desktop, but iOS needs notification permission and an installed app. It shows the person that the app has attention to give.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt on desktop Chrome and Edge; iOS requires Home Screen web app plus granted notifications.

ios_safari.note: Home Screen web apps with notification permission

chrome_android.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

samsung.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

limits.headline: Can show a number or dot on the icon of an installed web app
limits.user_action: You install a web app and, on iPhone, allow notifications
can: Show an unread count or dot on the app icon
Update the count while the app is open or when a push arrives
Clear the count when you open the item
cannot: Do this for a site that is not installed as an app
Do this on iPhone without notification permission
See what number is already showing
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on desktop need no pop up. iPhone needs a Home Screen web app plus allowed notifications. Firefox does not support it.

story.what_it_is: An installed web app can show a small number or dot on its icon.

marketing.name: Badging API
marketing.pitch: Installed web apps can set a badge on their icon to show new items, such as unread messages.

story.for_you: You see a number or dot on the app icon in your dock or home screen, like unread chats. It tells you something is waiting without a pop up.
story.for_makers: Makers use the badge to pull people back to the app. A small count can raise return visits. It is only for installed web apps, and works with push messages.

use_cases.example: A web chat app installed on your laptop shows a red 3 on its icon when three new messages arrive.
A web mail app shows the count of unread emails on its dock icon.
A browser game shows a dot when your turn arrives in an online board game.
A store web app shows a dot when your order ships or a deal drops.
A social web app shows a number for new replies and follows.
A task web app shows how many tasks are due today.
A news web app shows how many breaking stories you have not read.
